_doc: Steps for the live xLights kit wizard. One working sequence file; after each step the user saves and the wizard checks the file immediately. For a change step the wizard looks at the right-most effect of that type and compares it with both the previous step and the effect's defaults, keeping the smaller difference - so the user may keep editing the same effect or add a fresh copy for each step. Labels are from recent xLights; 'aka' gives alternate names. kit_version is bumped whenever the steps change; min_compatible is the oldest kit_version whose results can still be used as-is (older ones must be re-trained). 'xlights-kit --update' learns only the steps a version's training doesn't have yet (e.g. after a kit_version bump); a variant's 'needs' names another variant of the effect that must be done first (Pictures: the file), which --update then asks for again too.

effects.on: a model that HAS a singing face - the next step chooses one of its faces

variants.do: Face Definition: choose one of the model's faces (any face other than the one shown)

Phoneme Track (the timing track the face follows): choose a lyrics timing track. xLights only lists a timing track that has been broken down: add a timing track, type any words into one of its marks (or right-click it > Import Lyrics), then right-click the track > Breakdown Phrases and again > Breakdown Words; then choose it here
Filename (the file picker): choose any picture file - an animated GIF is best
Scaling: set it to No Scaling (choosing the file in the step before switched it to Scale To Fit by itself)
tick Loop GIF
tick Transparent Black
Frame Rate Adj (the GIF's speed): set to its maximum

structure.do: Add a Color Wash whose palette has exactly 3 colours enabled: pure red, pure green, pure blue.

On the same model, add a second effect layer (right-click the model's row > Insert Layer Above or Below - either is fine) and put any effect on the new layer, overlapping an effect on the other layer.
Add a Color Wash (defaults) to any model GROUP.
Add an effect to any model GROUP; in its Layer Settings (the Buffer tab) set Render Style to 'Per Model Default'.

On any effect, open the value curve of one of its sliders (the small button beside a slider, e.g. Bars' Palette Rep or Color Wash's Count): Type 'Ramp', the start at the slider's LOWEST value and the end at its HIGHEST; OK.
Open that value curve again and swap them: the start at the HIGHEST value, the end at the LOWEST; OK.
Open that value curve again: Type 'Custom'; click once in the middle of the curve to add a point and drag that point to the very TOP; OK.
On any effect: Layer Settings > the Roto-Zoom tab > the Z-axis rotation slider (it turns the effect flat, in the plane of the prop - not X or Y, which tilt it): drag it to its HIGHEST value.
Add a new timing track with at least 3 marks (any kind, any name - e.g. a metronome track).

Last step, and the only one on a submodel: add an On effect to a SUBMODEL row - in the sequencer, expand a model that has submodels (the small arrow next to its name) and put On on one of its submodel rows.
